How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One of the most frustrating processes since LA couldn't be signed digitally at UIT. Different bereaucratic systemst that don't communicate with each other is a complete disaster and such a drag for the applicant going through it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A thorough guide can be found online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: When writing e-mails asking for help people were definitely helpful, BUT their time could've probably been spend so much better than to answer the same questions over and over again just because the application system is so confusing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: More or less succesful. The package of courses I could attend was wrongly filled by the university, so one of the courses listed in the package didn't even exist and I had to find a replacement last minute. Luckily the replacement course proved to be one of the best during the stay, but still a hastle that it wasn't correctly informed the first time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Compared to KU the work load was significantly less, but teachers were extremely compentent and inspiring. It was nice to actually be able to read most of the stuff on the curriculum.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Somewhat the same but with a surprising absence of secondary literature/research papers to support the lectures. This had pros and cons, but for the most part it was liberating in this situation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: RUS-1110 & KVI-2512. Both very inspiring programmes with interesting lectures and very, very competent teachers.

questions.answer: Almost exactly the same as Danish culture, very easy transition.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: This one is tougher. Norwegians might be even more reserved than Danish people. A couple beverages usually let the shoulders sink, as we all know. Otherwise maybe meet them for an activity.
